data.narrative:
Furno Materials is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Gurinder Nagra that has raised $11M to date. The valuation universe comprises 9 comparable companies in Climate & Energy: 1 public equity (Lenza, ticker LNZA) and 8 private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Only one valuation method was applicable to this analysis. The Stage-Progression approach uses the $11M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression in venture capital, yielding an implied valuation of $28M. This approach is grounded in observed step-up patterns but does not incorporate company-specific metrics or peer comparison data.

The Peer-Median method was not applicable due to insufficient narrow peer comparables. While 8 same-sector peers exist, none met the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier; the analysis requires at least 3 datapoints to be meaningful. Reliance on the broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of climate-tech business models and capital intensity.

The triangulated valuation range is $23M–$32M, with a median of $28M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity band around the stage-progression result. The primary uncertainty stems from the single-method foundation; validation through revenue multiples, customer metrics, or technology-risk adjusted DCF analysis would strengthen conviction. Early-stage climate and energy companies exhibit wide valuation dispersion, limiting comp precision at the seed stage.
